questions.q: What exact method did Hartwell's compliance audit use to count standing admin access to the OT/SCADA segment?
options: A review of every individual IAM policy and Azure AD role assignment on the OT/SCADA boundary
Exporting and de-duplicating membership of the OT-SCADA-Admins and ot-scada-admins groups
A live interview with each account holder
Mara's Python inventory automation
questions.explain: The audit's documented method was a group membership export of OT-SCADA-Admins (Entra ID) and ot-scada-admins (AWS), de-duplicated and counted -- nothing else.

questions.q: What count did the audit report, as of its October 12 cutoff?
options: 19 accounts
9 accounts
14 accounts
5 accounts
questions.explain: The audit reported 14 accounts holding standing admin access to the OT/SCADA segment, based on group membership alone.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the audit's group-membership method as "completely normal," not a mistake?
options: Because group membership is literally how Hartwell's own access policy says privileged access to this segment is supposed to be granted
Because compliance auditors are never expected to check more than one data source
Because the audit team was told not to look any further
Because Azure AD groups cannot be queried any other way
questions.explain: Auditing against the documented policy's own named control -- group membership -- is the standard, defensible approach, which is exactly why it isn't framed as an error at this point in the story.

questions.q: What two groups did the auditor pull membership from?
options: SCADA-ReadOnly and ot-scada-viewers
OT-SCADA-Admins (Entra ID) and ot-scada-admins (AWS)
Global Administrators and root
IT-Support and ot-helpdesk
questions.explain: OT-SCADA-Admins is the Microsoft Entra ID security group; ot-scada-admins is its consolidated AWS counterpart from the Lesson 6 identity work.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize memorizing the exact number, method, and date together?
options: Because the final test requires reciting audit charters verbatim
Because every lesson through Lesson 18 refers back to this exact figure, method, and date when comparing it against a second, different number
Because the date determines which cloud provider is being audited
Because Howard Okonjo changes the scope every lesson
questions.explain: The next lesson introduces a second count, measured against the same access and the same day, that does not match -- so the audit's exact figures become the fixed baseline for every lesson that follows.
